THE UNDERSONG

what was heard
beneath the Chord,
C. 1142 to 1147.

Not to be sung.
Not to be read
aloud.

It began below
hearing. We found
it in the water
first: rings on a
still cup, in time
with nothing we
were playing.

We caught it in
shards and slowed
it. It is a voice.
It is very large
and very far down,
and it is singing
the Chord.

Not copying.
Learning. Each year
it sang more of it.
In C.1145 it sang
the Bass part
whole. Better than
we do.

The Soprano's key
is here with me in
the cell. The high
voice keeps watch
over what must not
be sung.

I have sealed the
shards in the
Archive's lowest
shelf. Do not play
them. When you
play them, it
listens back.

The Heart will be
silenced tonight.
Ysolde believes a
song that stops
cannot be learned.
I want to believe
her.

But I played the
last shard again
this evening, and
there was a pause
in it, where our
Chord ends, and
then it

ON THE MAKING
OF WARDENS

For the Keepers
who come after me.
Read once. Then
lock it away.

A Warden is not
built. It is grown
in the song, deep,
where the Chord is
loudest. It takes
forty years. Most
do not wake.

We grow them
without eyes. A
guardian that
looks can be
fooled. One that
listens cannot.

They are taught
one thing: the
Chord is right and
everything else is
a false note.
Find the false note
and silence it.

They are gentle
with the quiet.
A sleeping child
can lie against a
Warden's foot and
be safe as stone.

I have wondered
what a Warden would
do if the Chord
ever stopped. The
answer frightens
me too much to
write down.

So I will only
write this: never
stop the Chord
while a Warden
still stands.

They cannot be
told it is over.

THE CHARTER
OF AURELITH

Set down in the
first year of the
Chord, over the
spring that sings.

We came through the
gates into a world
with no sound in it.

Here a note does
not fade. Here we
will build a city
that never has to
stop singing.

I. The Heart shall
hold the Chord.
While it holds, the
lanterns burn, the
crystal grows and
the gates stay open.

II. Every voice is
a lantern. No one
in Aurelith sings
alone, and no one
is made to be
silent.

III. Listen first.
Speak second. In
the Plaza of the
Held Note, speak
not at all.

IV. Four gates for
four voices:
Soprano to the
north, Alto to the
east, Tenor to the
south, Bass to the
west. Their lights
shall stand so no
traveller is lost.

V. The river Vesper
is the Chord's own
water. Drink of it,
sail on it, and
never wall it in.

VI. The Wardens
guard the gates and
the Heart. They
answer to the
conductor alone.

VII. Should the
Chord ever fail,
the conductor alone
may call a Rest.

A rest is not an
ending. It is the
silence the next
note needs.

Sung and set in
stone, C. 1.

WHAT IS SUNG IS
NEVER LOST.

THE FOUR VOICES

The Chord is four
parts sung as one.
Aurelith has a
gate for each, and
each gate a light
that stands into
the sky.

SOPRANO, north.
The high voice
keeps watch. Its
beam is the palest.
The Last
Procession left
the city by it.

ALTO, east.
The warm voice
welcomes. Most
travellers come in
under its beam, and
the Arcade opens
to meet them.

TENOR, south.
The bright voice
carries. Its beam
reaches furthest;
the lighthouses on
the plains were
tuned from it.

BASS, west.
The deep voice
holds. Its beam is
the darkest and the
steadiest. In every
chord the bass is
the floor the
others stand on.

Four statues face
the Heart, one for
each voice. Their
faces are blank so
anyone may sing in
them.

A chord is raised
as a house is: the
floor first, the
roof last. Deep,
bright, warm, high.
Sung any other way
it falls.

The Alto keeps the
lamplighters' song:
the hearth, the
river, the Chord,
the hearth again.
The Hall's cabinet
was tuned to it.

The fourth voice
points down.
It always has.
